knowledge:
- key_parameters: minCounts=Minimum read counts required for a gene to be kept ;; fSample=Minimum fraction of samples that must meet the minCounts threshold ;; hyper=Set to "yes" to filter out hypervariant genes based on coefficient of variation (CV) ;; th.cv=CV threshold for hypervariant gene filtering (default is 3) ;; type=Normalization method, either "vst" (default, fast) or "rlog" (very slow) ;; th.corr=Correlation threshold to identify and remove outlier samples (default is 0.9) in DaMiR.sampleFilt, or for feature selection/reduction in DaMiR.FSelect/DaMiR.FReduct ;; n.sv=Number of surrogate variables to use for batch effect adjustment ;; n.pred=Number of top predictors to select in DaMiR.FBest
- alternatives: type="rlog" in DaMiR.normalization is an alternative to type="vst" (VST is highly preferred for larger datasets due to speed) ;; method in DaMiR.SV can be "fve" (Fraction of Explained Variance, default), "be", or "leek" (from the sva package)
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have raw RNA-Seq count data and want to identify a small, robust set of transcriptional biomarkers and build classification models (binary or multi-class) while adjusting for batch effects and unwanted variation.
- pitfalls: Do not use normalized counts as input; DaMiRseq expects raw, un-normalized integer counts ;; Avoid using type="rlog" on large datasets as it is computationally expensive and can take hours ;; Ensure surrogate variables used for adjustment do not correlate with the biological class of interest to avoid overcorrection ;; Standard correlation analysis (DaMiR.corrplot) can be misleading for multi-level categorical variables (>2 levels, non-ordinal); use linear regression (lm()) instead to assess their relationship with surrogate variables.

workflows.name: standard_pipeline_and_classification
workflows.intent: Perform raw count normalization, sample filtering, surrogate variable adjustment, feature selection, and ensemble learning classification.
workflows.stages: 1. Import data and create a SummarizedExperiment object ;; 2. Filter and normalize counts ;; 3. Filter out low-correlation samples ;; 4. Identify and adjust for surrogate variables ;; 5. Transpose and perform feature selection and reduction ;; 6. Sort and select the best predictors ;; 7. Train and evaluate an ensemble classifier
workflows.code:
# count_data <- read.delim(filecounts)
# covariate_data <- read.delim(filecovariates, stringAsFactor = T)
# SE<-DaMiR.makeSE(count_data, covariate_data)
data(SE)
data_norm <- DaMiR.normalization(SE, minCounts=10, fSample=0.7, hyper = "yes", th.cv=3)
data_filt <- DaMiR.sampleFilt(data_norm, th.corr=0.9)
sv <- DaMiR.SV(data_filt)
data_adjust<-DaMiR.SVadjust(data_filt, sv, n.sv=4)
DaMiR.Allplot(data_adjust, colData(data_adjust))
set.seed(12345)
data_clean<-DaMiR.transpose(assay(data_adjust))
df<-colData(data_adjust)
data_reduced <- DaMiR.FSelect(data_clean, df, th.corr=0.4)
data_reduced <- DaMiR.FReduct(data_reduced$data)
DaMiR.MDSplot(data_reduced, df)
df.importance <- DaMiR.FSort(data_reduced, df)
selected_features <- DaMiR.FBest(data_reduced, ranking=df.importance, n.pred = 5)
DaMiR.Clustplot(selected_features$data, df)
Classification_res <- DaMiR.EnsembleLearning(selected_features$data, classes=df$class, fSample.tr = 0.5, fSample.tr.w = 0.5, iter = 30)

workflows.name: cross_validation_and_independent_prediction
workflows.intent: Train and test classification models inside a cross-validation loop, select the best model, normalize/adjust an independent test set, and predict classes.
workflows.stages: 1. Split data into learning and independent test sets ;; 2. Normalize and adjust the learning set ;; 3. Perform feature selection, model training, and testing inside a cross-validation loop ;; 4. Select the best model ;; 5. Normalize and adjust the independent test set using learning set parameters ;; 6. Predict classes on the adjusted independent test set
workflows.code:
data(SE)
idx_test <- c(18,19,39,40)
Ind_Test_set <- SE[, idx_test, drop=FALSE]
Learning_set <- SE[, -idx_test, drop=FALSE]
data_norm <- DaMiR.normalization(Learning_set, minCounts=10, fSample=0.7, hyper = "yes", th.cv=3)
sv <- DaMiR.SV(data_norm)
data_adjust <- DaMiR.SVadjust(data_norm, sv, n.sv=4)
expr_LearningSet <- Learning_set[rownames(data_norm)]
expr_Ind_Test_set <- Ind_Test_set[rownames(data_norm)]
norm_ind_ts <- DaMiR.iTSnorm(expr_LearningSet, expr_Ind_Test_set, normtype = "vst", method = "precise")
adj_norm_ind_ts <- DaMiR.iTSadjust(data_adjust, norm_ind_ts)
